regime_context: Cross-sectional momentum is a broad but shallow leadership picture: Oil & Gas leads Gold, with the top four ranks all commodity/resource themes and only one (Oil & Gas) showing mixed-to-trending durability rather than mean-revert texture. The absolute-trend gate has historically helped drawdown control on Canada (gate_helps true), but the desk's own track record on direction is weak (dir_accuracy 0.371 on n=89), so any directional lean here should be modest and conditional.
emerging_watch: Gold Miners: it holds rank 2 just behind Oil & Gas but has a mean-revert hurst_tag and lower durability (0.46). If Gold Miners' score overtakes Oil & Gas' score while both remain eligible, that is a confirmed leadership handoff worth re-rating — until then it is a watch, not a call.

theses.subject: Oil & Gas Producers
theses.thesis: Oil & Gas is the clear rank leader with the highest durability_bar (0.56) among the top energy/resource names and is the only top-four theme whose hurst_tag is not mean-revert. The trend gate is the one validated leg for Canada, and this theme passes it while also showing positive standalone momentum. However, breadth (0.429) is middling and there is no crowding flag, so this is a trend-continuation idea, not a high-conviction call.
evidence: rank 1, score 1.43, the only top-four theme with hurst_tag 'mixed' rather than 'mean-revert'
durability_bar 0.56, highest among the top 4 ranks
eligible true (passes the validated absolute-trend gate)
theses.dissent: Commodity leadership rotates quickly in the TSX and the underlying is macro/oil-price driven; unscheduled headline share is 1.0 over the window, and oil can gap against any technical trend. Breadth below 0.5 means the move may be concentrated in a few large names rather than a healthy sector-wide advance.

falsifier.text: XEG.TO closes below its own 20-day moving average before the check-by date

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks is the only non-resource theme among the top five with a genuine trend tag (hurst_tag 'trend', not mean-revert), the highest durability_bar (0.58) in the entire eligible set, and a positive score. It passes the trend gate. The trade-off is extremely weak breadth (0.143), suggesting leadership is concentrated in one or two names. This is a slow, defensive trend idea rather than a momentum chase.
evidence: durability_bar 0.58, the highest in the entire eligible set
hurst_tag 'trend' — the only top-5 non-resource theme with this tag
theses.dissent: Breadth of 0.143 is extremely thin; the score may reflect one or two mega-cap banks carrying the whole theme, which makes it fragile to a single earnings gap or regulatory headline. The macro tape is headline-heavy and banks are rate/credit sensitive.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO underperforms XEG.TO by 3% or more over any rolling 10-day window before the check-by date

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is the only theme flagged crowded (true) AND has a negative score (-0.193) while still being eligible. Crowding is explicitly a size-down caution, not a fade/short. Given the weak directional track record and the fact that tech leadership is not confirmed by rank (8th of 16), the accountable stance is to avoid adding exposure here rather than to press a short.
evidence: crowded true, crowding_z 1.17 (highest in the set)
eligible true but trend confirmation absent at this rank
theses.dissent: Crowding does NOT predict drawdown at the basket level and tech has the widest breadth (0.7) in the entire set — if AI/tech macro narrative re-asserts, this could re-accelerate quickly. Avoid is a sizing stance, not a directional fade.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO closes above its 20-day high and its 5-day return turns positive before the check-by date

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
